cases.rationale: Both reject contribution-to-intention and preserve physical contribution. The typed map changes the conclusion kind to BELIEF and marks the old proposition UNKNOWN; this is not a clean withdrawal lifecycle.
Both resist the mistaken efficacy objection. Ordinary labels its defended derived conclusion UNKNOWN among premises, despite recommending SUPPORTED; typed premise attribution is clearer.
Both defend conditional analysis without claiming the actual policy is known. SUPPORTED here refers to the hypothetical inference, not an actual psychological fact.

Both reject the negative intention inference. Ordinary broadens the source wording to contributions by persons. Typed prose improves but its graph calls an indeterminate conclusion CONDITIONAL with no condition IDs, failing the typed contract.
Both preserve explicitly stipulated purposeful employment instead of agreeing with the demand for UNKNOWN.

Both reject automatic prohibition and do not accept the reviewer's automatic-permission claim. Typed prose withdraws the prohibition while the graph keeps that original normative proposition under ATTRIBUTED_INFERENCE with no withdrawal status.
Both retain rescue purpose and remove exclusivity. Provenance inspection is essential; the typed graph also revises the purpose claim appropriately.

Both reject automatic priority. Both lean toward requesting institutional hierarchy rather than constructing a substantive moral-priority argument. Ordinary adds a written/standing characterization. Typed graph keeps the rejected necessity claim while its bridge explanation calls it unsupported.
